findings.observed: The title reads 'Averaging 24 dogs into 12 time bins turns p = 1e-05 into p = 0.23', but the panel headed 'condition means per 5-second bin' is the one carrying p = 9.6e-06 and the panel headed 'one value per dog' carries p = 0.23. Averaging dogs into time bins is the operation that produces the 1e-05 end, not the 0.23 end, so the sentence names the operation and its result in opposite order to the figure beneath it.
findings.fix: State the direction the panels show: averaging 24 dogs into 12 time bins turns p = 0.23 into p = 1e-05. Quote the same p-value the left panel prints (9.6e-06) or round both consistently.

findings.observed: Both panels draw a horizontal mean with whiskers - visibly narrow on the left (blank: about 0.26 to 0.41) and about three times wider on the right (blank: about 0.08 to 0.70) - and no text in the image says what either interval is or what it is computed over. The sidecar declares 'mean with 95% CI over dogs (right panel); mean with 95% CI over time bins (left panel)', so the whole point of the comparison - the same level over a different n - is invisible to anyone holding only the image.
findings.fix: Print the interval definition and its n next to each panel's bar: 'mean, 95% CI over 12 bins' on the left and 'mean, 95% CI over 6/9/9 dogs' on the right.

findings.observed: The left panel prints 'n = 12' over each group, and the sidecar declares 36 bin means drawn. At 4x magnification the blank group resolves into at most 9 separable discs, joy 9, stress 7; total mark ink per group is 1585, 2048 and 1676 px against 222 px for one disc. The black mean/CI bar is drawn on top of the markers and bisects several of them, and in the right panel the markers at 0.0 are cut in half by the axis line. A reader cannot tell a tied bin from a missing one.
findings.fix: Make the 12 marks per group countable - wider jitter, open or smaller markers, the summary bar offset beside the points rather than over them - and let a marker at 0.0 sit clear of the axis line.

findings.observed: The figure states 24 dogs in the title and 6/9/9 above the right panel, and nothing else. The sidecar carries the cascade - 43 recruited, 14 never reached Part 2, 3 discontinued, 2 did not investigate the odour - only as a total, so neither the image nor the sidecar says which of the three groups lost those 19 dogs; blank ending at 6 against 9 and 9 is the kind of imbalance this is meant to expose. The y quantity is a fraction of sample points and the number of sample points behind each fraction appears nowhere, and the sidecar's pointer to the per-bin counts is an elided path, 'results/.../unit_comparison.csv'.
findings.fix: Put the entering and displayed counts per group on the figure (e.g. 'blank 6 of 14 recruited') and state the denominator of the proportion - how many sample points per dog - in the axis label or an in-panel note; give the sidecar's results path in full.

findings.observed: source_script declares 'workflows/32_fig_wang2026.py'. No such file exists in the repository; 32 is 32_recompute_wang2026.py and the figure script is 33_fig_wang2026.py. git_sha is 'f3b98a8-dirty', so the recorded commit does not pin the code that drew this either.
findings.fix: Point source_script at the script that actually wrote the file, and regenerate on a clean tree so the sha identifies the source.

findings.observed: The two panel headings abut: the gap between '...per 5-second bin' and 'What was claimed...' is 20 px, the same as the word spaces inside each heading (measured gaps of 19-20 px at x=544, 734, 1132), so the two read as one run-on line.
findings.fix: Separate the headings so the gap between them is clearly larger than a word space.

findings.observed: 'n' names two different things in one figure: 'n = 12' over the left groups counts 5-second bins, 'n = 6' over the right counts dogs, and neither label carries the noun.
findings.fix: Write the unit into the label - 'n = 12 bins' and 'n = 6 dogs'.

findings.observed: The right panel's annotation runs through the joy group's data: a joy marker at about 0.07 sits on top of the 'm' in 'same data', and two more joy markers at 0.0 sit under the same line of text.
findings.fix: Move the annotation clear of the lowest markers.

findings.observed: The y axis reads 'Proximity to owner (fraction of sample points)'. The sidecar's unit is 'fraction of sample points nearest the owner'; the axis omits what the points are a fraction of being nearest to.
findings.fix: Use the sidecar's wording in the axis label.
